children.label: Introduction
children.text: A carrier can be practical and still say something about its owner. Porter Luxury Carriers is a South African accessible-premium brand established in 2021, offering leather, woven and knitted bags and accessories. Its range includes hobos, shoppers, clutches, pouches, straps and personalised products. This project explores how Porter can translate expressive colour, everyday versatility and personalisation into a digital experience that attracts attention and gives customers confidence to purchase.

children.label: Methodology
children.text: This project combines secondary research with primary data collected through a short Google Forms survey. The survey provides exploratory insight into respondents’ perceptions and preferences relevant to Porter’s digital marketing. The sample size, collection dates, questions and aggregate findings are documented alongside the results. Findings from a small convenience sample are directional and should not be generalised to Porter’s entire target market.

children.label: Limitations
children.text: Exploratory convenience sample; findings are directional and cannot be generalised to all Porter customers.

children.label: Insights introduction
children.text: The analysis brings together secondary research, documented digital observations and primary research collected through Google Forms. These inputs inform a proposed customer profile and digital journey. Survey findings describe the respondents who participated; they do not establish the preferences of all Porter customers.

children.label: Proposed primary profile
children.text: Expressive Everyday Professionals, provisionally aligned with Eighty20’s Middle Class Workers segment.

children.label: Targeting choices
children.text: Employed, digitally connected South African women approximately 25-55, particularly in urban Western Cape and Gauteng, seeking distinctive design, versatility, quality and credible value. Age, geography and segment alignment are proposed targeting choices. The ENS segment is not exclusively female; alignment is not established by Porter transactions.

children.label: Measurement introduction
children.text: This dashboard sets out proposed 12-month targets for Porter’s digital strategy. Targets are planning assumptions to be validated against the brand’s baseline performance, budget, stock availability and operating capacity. They are not industry benchmarks or claims about current results. Performance should be monitored monthly and reviewed quarterly.

children.label: Monthly comparison
children.text: Compare the final 30 days with a documented 30-day launch baseline. Use like-for-like definitions and consider seasonality.

children.label: Follower objective
children.text: Increase Porter’s Instagram following by 25%, from the student-reported baseline of approximately 15,600 to 19,500 followers by 8 September 2027, subject to confirming the exact starting count.

children.label: Caveat
children.text: Student-reported approximate starting count. Follower count does not prove audience relevance or sales.

children.label: Revenue objective
children.text: Increase net online sales revenue during 8 September 2026 - 7 September 2027 by at least 20% compared with 8 September 2025 - 7 September 2026.

children.label: Summary
children.text: The principal barriers are uncertain quality and capacity, unclear stock and service information, and premium value without proof. A connected, content-led journey should make expressive design discoverable and reduce practical uncertainty.

children.label: Recommendation
children.text: Porter should use a focused, content-led digital strategy in which Instagram creates discovery, the website supplies proof and enables conversion, email supports retention, and customer advocacy strengthens future discovery.
